$comment: Reading prompts for the voice recorder. Aim to record ALL of these — ~40 short sentences gives ~4-6 minutes of clean audio, enough for a solid XTTS fine-tune. Read naturally, at a normal pace, in a quiet room. The text of each prompt becomes the transcript in metadata.csv, so read it EXACTLY as written (punctuation guides your intonation).
prompts: The morning light came slowly through the tall windows.
She set the cup down and turned another page.
There was no hurry, and the room was very quiet.
Rain had been falling since before dawn.
He read the same line three times before it made sense.
The old clock in the hall kept its patient time.
Outside, the street was almost empty.
A single lamp burned in the corner of the study.
The words seemed to settle as she spoke them aloud.
Nothing moved except the smoke from the chimney.
I remember the smell of paper and rain that afternoon.
The chapter ended, and she closed the book gently.
Wind pushed the last dry leaves along the pavement.
He wrote a short note and left it on the table.
The station was quiet between the trains.
Snow had covered the garden overnight.
She listened to the house settle around her.
The kettle clicked off and the room went still again.
Every sentence seemed to have room to breathe.
A dog barked twice, far off, then stopped.
The map was folded so many times it had begun to tear.
He counted the coins twice and put them away.
Light moved across the wall as the afternoon went on.
The letter had taken nine days to arrive.
She spoke slowly, as if reading to a child.
The fire had burned down to a soft orange glow.
They walked without speaking for a long while.
The bell above the door rang as he came inside.
A thin mist hung over the fields until noon.
The page was dense with small, careful handwriting.
He paused at the window and watched the harbour.
The house was older than anyone could quite remember.
She marked her place with a strip of blue ribbon.
The lecture ran long, and the light outside failed.
Somewhere upstairs a door opened and closed.
The tea had gone cold but he drank it anyway.
Numbers filled the margin in faded pencil.
The road curved away between two low hills.
It was the kind of silence that asks nothing of you.
She finished the last line and set down her pen.
